name: 나라 선택
description: 큰 지형 덩어리와 자연스러운 국경으로 나라를 구분하고, 선택한 나라에서 지역 살펴보기로 이어집니다.
prompt:
Create a completely redesigned FIRST screen of the TownGrid new-game start flow. This is ONE high-fidelity Korean game UI image mockup, 16:9, large and crisp, not a collage or poster. The attached two images are the APPROVED second and third screens; match their pixel art language and understated dark-teal / cream / orange interface family, but this new screen is a WORLD / COUNTRY overview many times farther zoomed out. Do not modify or reproduce those two approved screens.

The user REJECTED the prior first-screen composition: a rigid diamond-shaped continent with a continuous mountain fence around its edge, too much blue inland water, thousands of noisy little props, labels in heavy teal plaques, and three dropdown rectangles across the top. Rebuild both the geography composition and the UI. This must visibly be a NEW DESIGN.

ART DIRECTION: A calm, spacious, coherent inhabited CONTINENT, viewed from a fixed orthographic isometric quarter view, approximately 35 degrees above the land. The continuous LAND FILLS THE ENTIRE VIEWPORT edge to edge; its land extends beyond the four edges. No floating diamond, no detached map slab, no visible rectangular world edge, no enclosing ocean. This is a continent-wide zoom level with broad large biomes and nations, not individual house tiles. Keep crafted pixel art, large readable color clusters and crisp stepped edges. Avoid smooth realistic 3D, painterly watercolor, parchment, perspective depth or a hazy horizon. Significantly LESS visual clutter and tiny details than either reference.

GEOGRAPHY — a fresh, natural macro layout:
- Upper-left and far upper center: TWO short, irregular broken mountain ranges with snowy summits, valleys and real gaps. Mountains cover at most 15% of the visible image. Never a continuous straight wall or symmetrical perimeter.
- Broad open green RIVER PLAINS occupy the center and left-middle; clustered dark forest occupies the west side in a few distinct masses with open clearings.
- A medium-width winding river runs from the northern valleys through the middle in a graceful S, branching into a modest irregular THREE-ARM inland lake, slightly right of center. The lake plus all water occupies only 12-15% of the screen. One small frosty bay upper-right and a warm lagoon lower-right are subordinate, not giant seas. Land remains one connected continent.
- Eastern rolling highlands are greener and a little stonier; the bottom-left has a wide dry ochre plateau transitioning naturally from grassland. A small dark volcanic patch far north is optional. Show gradual biome transitions, no colored rectangular bands.
- 14 irregular political territories exist on this larger connected land, FOUR large and TEN small, separated by thin restrained borders that follow riverbanks, mountain ridges and believable landmarks. No checkerboard of visible plot grid at this zoom. Leave a meaningful southwestern wilderness with no nation border.
- At most 9 very SMALL distinctive settlement/capital sprite clusters TOTAL: one modest castle city in central plains, small forest town in west, mountain forge town north-west, a rail/factory city in east, a few little trading settlements near waterways. No repeated icons carpeting the landscape. Capitals occupy only a few percent of screen.
- Use ample calm open land between these landmarks. Pixel art can be attractive without every square centimeter having a prop.

COUNTRY READABILITY:
The selected central-left plains territory is "에스테른 왕국". Give ONLY this nation a subtle warm cream highlight and crisp muted golden boundary; this is a broad multi-plot country, not a single square plot. Its boundary should be natural and irregular, not diamond-shaped. Mark its small capital with one tiny cream pennant.
Country names sit DIRECTLY on the map in restrained dark ink with a thin light halo, NO rectangles or plaques. Main labels about 22px, secondary about 15px. Four major name labels: "에스테른 왕국" center-left, "아르셀 연방" right-middle, "네자르 마도국" upper area, "오르벨 왕국" lower-left edge. The latter two are hostile, add a small unobtrusive lock beside those names, no scary giant warning overlays. Four small readable labels placed with clear spacing: "실바엔 숲공국", "카르둠 산악공국", "리벤트 자유시", "브로덴 철도시". Other small territory names may appear as tiny unobtrusive marks, no invented names. The center-right small inland lake can have ONE subdued water label "유리 내해". Labels never overlap UI, towns, or each other.

REDESIGNED MINIMAL UI — FEW ELEMENTS, CLEAR ACTION:
Top-left: a compact 40px dark-teal back-arrow square followed by a clean 24px dark-teal title on a softly quiet patch of landscape, "어디에서 시작할까요?". Directly beneath, just ONE small muted line, "지도에서 나라를 고르세요". This is not a banner panel. Do not repeat a big logo, stepper, breadcrumbs, or 3 dropdowns.
Top-right: ONE quiet flat dark-teal button "지형으로 찾기" with a small simple search icon. That is all at the top right.
Bottom-center: ONE low-profile FLAT dark-teal #193f42 floating horizontal selection strip, approx 700px wide and 82px high at 1672px canvas width; corners 3px. Left small simple shield icon, bold cream "에스테른 왕국", below a single concise muted line "평야 · 숲 · 하천". Right exactly ONE primary ORANGE #ee701b button labeled "지역 살펴보기 →". The strip is aligned and generously padded, not segmented into many cards, no metallic bevels, no glowing frames, no close X, no stats, no resource icons. The button means zoom into the selected nation, leading to approved Screen 2, NOT instantly start the game.
Bottom-right, well clear of the selection strip: two tiny understated minus and plus controls in one slim teal group.
No right sidebar, no bottom card carousel, no legends, no progress bars, no gameplay HUD, no giant compass. One selected nation and one clear next action.

FINISH: A premium, approachable, restrained pixel strategy-game country-selection screen. More readable and spatially composed, lower detail density, calmer natural land organization. The new geographical layout is a concept proposal, not required to match old borders or old land shape. Korean text precisely as provided.
